title: Simple Circuits
ques: If you have a battery, a small light bulb, and one piece of wire, how do you connect them so the bulb lights up?

answer.content: You must create a complete circle (a circuit). You touch the bottom of the bulb to one end of the battery. Then, you use the wire to connect the side of the bulb to the other end of the battery.

explanation: This tests practical knowledge of how a basic electrical circuit operates.

title: Conductors and Insulators
ques: Which of these materials will allow electricity to pass through it: a metal paperclip or a rubber eraser?

answer.content: The **metal paperclip** will allow electricity to pass through it because metals are good **conductors**. The rubber eraser is an **insulator** and blocks electricity.

explanation: This distinguishes between materials that permit electron flow and those that resist it.

title: Electrical Safety
ques: Why is it very dangerous to touch electrical appliances, like a toaster or a hairdryer, with wet hands?

answer.content: It is dangerous because water (especially tap water) is a good conductor of electricity. If your hands are wet, electricity can travel easily from the appliance, through the water, and into your body, giving you a severe shock.

explanation: This applies electrical principles to critical home safety.
